work_section.title: Selected case studies
work_section.subtitle: Three projects with measurable business and operational impact

cards.title: Automated Fundraiser Acknowledgment at Scale
cards.summary: Replaced a manual outsourced workflow for thanking fundraisers with browser automation that executed reliably and continuously.
cards.outcome: Delivered 12x per-operator throughput and ran 72 parallel workers, eliminating backlog while reducing response errors.
highlights: Handled workloads spanning tens of thousands of monthly fundraiser pages
Improved response speed enough to increase fundraiser chat engagement
Reduced operational overhead previously spent managing manual queues

cards.title: Built Realtime Fundraiser Creation + Donation Visibility
cards.summary: Shipped a web app that enabled one-click fundraiser creation and immediate donation insight, replacing lagging batch CSV processes.
cards.outcome: Moved teams from delayed, donation-only reporting to realtime operational visibility across millions of users and tens of millions of donation records.
highlights: Integrated Meta APIs to capture fundraiser creation at the source
Enabled immediate donation context for customer-facing chat teams
Improved decision quality for sales, success, and analytics teams

crate_section.title: Open-source proof of how I think
crate_section.subtitle: These crates show the engineering traits I optimize for: explicit invariants, readable APIs, and architecture that makes incorrect states harder to express.

cards.name: statum
cards.summary: Compile-time typestate patterns for Rust systems where transitions, staged construction, and persistence need to stay explicit.
highlights: Makes invalid transitions impossible to represent at the type level
Supports reconstructing machines from persisted data without dropping type safety
Reflects my bias toward APIs that encode workflow rules instead of documenting them

cards.name: nestum
cards.summary: Nested enum paths and match ergonomics for domains where hierarchy is real and flattening the model makes code harder to read.
highlights: Lets APIs read like the problem domain, such as Event::Documents::Update
Keeps nested invariants visible instead of hiding them behind conversion layers
Shows my preference for abstractions that remove friction without weakening meaning

cards.name: modum
cards.summary: A Rust workspace lint tool for naming, namespace shape, and API-surface rules that I want codebases to hold consistently.
highlights: Turns readability and API-shape standards into an enforceable workspace check
Carries the same type-first, module-first standards used throughout this portfolio
